title: SyntaxError
kicker: Python for SDFs · Fix the error
code:
doc_types = ["Cover Letter", "Certificate of Quality", "BSE/TSE Declaration"]
for doc_type in doc_types
    print(doc_type)

notes.label: SyntaxError
notes.text: The type of error. Python couldn't read the cell as Python, so none of it ran, not even line 1.

notes.label: expected ':'
notes.text: The reason. Python expected a colon. A `for` line has to end with `:`.

notes.label: line 2, and the ^
notes.text: A SyntaxError has no ----> arrow. The line at the top names the line number, and the ^ marks where Python got stuck: the end of line 2.

fixes.label: for doc_type in doc_types:
fixes.title: Best fix
fixes.feedback: A `for` line ends with a colon. With it in place, the loop prints the three document types, one per line.

fixes.label: for doc_type in doc_types;
fixes.title: Still a SyntaxError
fixes.feedback: A semicolon isn't a colon. Python still can't tell where the loop line ends and the repeated part starts.

fixes.label: for doc_type in doc_types
fixes.title: A new error, same missing colon
fixes.feedback: Pushing line 2 in gives you an IndentationError (unexpected indent), and the colon is still missing. The spaces were fine. The colon was the problem.
fixes.fixed_code:
doc_types = ["Cover Letter", "Certificate of Quality", "BSE/TSE Declaration"]
    for doc_type in doc_types
    print(doc_type)

_note: traceback from IPython 7.34 / Python 3.12 (kernel output, only the temp-file path shortened to <ipython-input-2>); confirm against a live Colab run. SyntaxError and IndentationError are reported before the cell runs, so IPython prints a File/line header and a ^ caret instead of a ----> arrow
